page: Microsoft Azure HB368-192rs_v5 is a high-performance computing virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture. Configured under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance provides 192 dedicated vCPUs paired with 448.0 GB of system memory. This resource profile yields approximately 2.33 GB of RAM per vCPU, aligning with compute-dense scenarios that prioritize processing parallelism over expansive per-core memory capacities.

A notable hardware aspect of the HB368-192rs_v5 is the local storage configuration, featuring 15,874 GB of integrated NVMe SSD capacity. The platform also natively supports RDMA-capable networking and Premium Storage integration, catering to tightly coupled, latency-sensitive clustered environments. The architecture contains no physical GPUs or dedicated accelerator units.

From an infrastructure cost efficiency perspective, the hardware density combines massive parallel compute capacity with a high-capacity local NVMe array. Organizations running workloads with high temporary scratch space demands eliminate the necessity for standalone attached storage volumes. However, with 2.33 GB per core, workloads bound by high memory footprints per thread must account for the constrained memory-to-core allocation.

The HB368-192rs_v5 is engineered for large-scale distributed computational tasks. Target applications include computational fluid dynamics, finite element analysis, weather modeling, seismic data processing, and large-scale parallel simulations requiring fast low-latency interconnects and dense local intermediate scratch I/O.
description: Microsoft Azure HB368-192rs_v5 is a high-performance computing instance powered by a dedicated 192-vCPU x86_64 Intel architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 448.0 GB of RAM, offering a compute-focused ratio of 2.33 GB per core. The server integrates a substantial local storage array of 15,874 GB across NVMe SSDs, alongside support for RDMA networking and Premium Storage attachments. With no discrete GPU acceleration, the hardware configuration is optimized for parallel processing throughput and high-speed temporary disk scratch performance. The relatively lower memory-to-core balance positions this instance strategically for scalable, distributed compute jobs rather than in-memory data caches. HB368-192rs_v5 is well suited for engineering simulations, computational fluid dynamics, molecular dynamics modeling, and heavy batch processing requiring low-latency clustering and intensive local file input and output.
